page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. The instance supplies 128 virtual CPUs derived from 64 physical cores using two threads per core. Memory capacity measures 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4:1 ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The underlying hardware incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

Hardware benchmark testing indicates exceptional throughput across heavily threaded computing tasks. The server achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU tests (106,176.97) and extended instruction sets (154,805.89), alongside top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 702.64 GB/sec. Memory read operations in cached blocks achieve 8,778.99 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads reach 508.63 GB/sec and writes sustain 218.52 GB/sec. Furthermore, the instance handles 157.89 million Redis SET operations per second and demonstrates strong multi-core scaling in Geekbench and Clang compilation.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe or ephemeral storage, requiring attached network storage volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file management. It also contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs. While single-thread benchmarks place in average to strong categories, the sheer core count delivers high multi-threaded density. The inclusion of AMX hardware units allows the instance to process CPU-bound inference workloads, achieving 41.27 tokens per second on large 70B parameter models during prompt evaluation.

Microsoft Azure D128s_v6 is optimized for large-scale enterprise deployments requiring high concurrency and balanced compute-to-memory footprints. Its resource profile aligns with large relational databases, in-memory caches, high-throughput static web serving, Clang build farms, batch processing pipelines, and data transformations.

The processor integrates 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced execution extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on remote network storage volumes for data retention.
